root_cause.text: The loop over pending catchall elements was prematurely terminated after processing the first viable candidate due to `break` statements, preventing proper cleanup of all catchall elements when a set is being destroyed during transaction processing.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes two `break` statements from the `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` and `nft_map_catchall_activate()` functions. These breaks caused the loops to exit after handling only the first catchall element, leaving subsequent pending catchall elements unprocessed. When a set containing multiple catchall elements (one live and one pending from a new batch) is destroyed, the unprocessed elements trigger the warning in `nft_data_release()` due to improper reference counting during abort handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature loop termination to ensure all catchall elements are deactivated instead of only the first one.
intent_record.what: Removed a `break;` statement that was the last line inside a loop body before the closing brace of a `do-while` or `for` loop in the nft_map_catchall_deactivate function.
intent_record.how: This removal allows the loop to continue iterating instead of terminating after the first iteration. The loop will now process all remaining elements rather than exiting after handling the first catchall element, enabling complete deactivation of all catchall entries in the set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature loop termination to ensure all catchall elements are processed during activation.
intent_record.what: Removed a `break;` statement from the end of a for-loop body in the `nft_map_catchall_activate()` function.
intent_record.how: This change allows the loop to continue iterating through remaining elements instead of terminating after processing the first catchall element. Previously, the break would exit the loop after one iteration; now the loop will process all iterations until its natural termination condition.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in the `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` function introduced in this commit. At lines 34-39 of the diff, the function iterates over catchall elements with `list_for_each_entry()` but contains a `break` statement at line 38 that terminates the loop after processing the first active catchall element. This prevents proper cleanup of all catchall elements when a set is being destroyed. The comment in the root cause explicitly states 'The loop over pending catchall elements was prematurely terminated after processing the first viable candidate due to `break` statements, preventing proper cleanup of all catchall elements.' The same premature `break` issue exists in `nft_map_catchall_activate()` at lines 63-68. This is a bug-introducing commit because it adds the vulnerable construct (the `break` statement that should not be there) rather than fixing it.

The code added in this commit introduces new stateful object infrastructure with functions like `nft_flush_table()` that includes a `list_for_each_entry_safe(obj, ne, &ctx->table->objects, list)` loop (lines 773-777), but this loop does NOT contain any `break` statements that would prematurely terminate it. Additionally, the vulnerability description mentions 'catchall elements' which are not present in this code - this commit adds generic stateful object support, not catchall-specific logic. Since the vulnerable construct (premature break in a catchall cleanup loop) is completely absent from this commit, has_bug=false.
